name: Hori
overview: Hori is a male Edomite figure identified in Scripture as the son of Lotan. His mention is brief and primarily genealogical, situating him within the Edomite lineage. There are no additional notes or details provided about his life or character.
namesAndTitles: The name Hori is a proper name meaning 'cave-dweller.' This meaning is given in the Hebrew context and is noted in Genesis 36:22. The name itself does not carry any divine attribution or special title beyond its literal meaning.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Hori is the son of Lotan, establishing his immediate family connection. No other family relationships are documented in the biblical text beyond this father-son relationship.
scriptureSignificance: Hori's significance lies in his place within the genealogical records of the Edomites, descendants of Esau, which helps trace the lineage and tribal divisions important in the biblical narrative. While not a prominent character in terms of actions or teachings, his inclusion preserves the historical and tribal identity that God allowed to exist within the broader story of His people.
